title: Metropolis Street Racer
subtitle: Driving with something to prove
summary: Metropolis Street Racer is Bizarre Creations' racing game, first released for Dreamcast in the United Kingdom on 3 November 2000.
body: Metropolis Street Racer is Bizarre Creations' racing game, first released for Dreamcast in the United Kingdom on 3 November 2000. Its routes run through recreations of London, Tokyo and San Francisco, with challenges that reward stylish driving as well as speed. The Kudos system measures that performance, turning a well-controlled slide or a clean finish into progress towards another event. Streets are closed into different courses within the cities, giving familiar junctions new uses as the campaign advances. Winning means showing command of the car, not merely reaching the next corner first.

Challenges award Kudos for completing their objectives and for the way the player drives. Drifting can increase the total, while collisions with scenery or other cars can reduce it. The player can also make certain tasks harder, such as reducing a time allowance, to increase the potential reward. That choice makes difficulty part of preparing the attempt. A spectacular corner becomes worthwhile only if it can be completed cleanly, so the scoring system repeatedly asks whether the extra risk will improve the run or undo its earlier progress.

The console's clock determines the time of day in each city, giving a drive through Tokyo a different light from one through London. Richard Jacques composed music for nine fictional radio stations, three associated with each location. Progress unlocks cars and courses for additional modes, extending the use of the city routes. Bizarre later developed Project Gotham Racing for Xbox from related ideas. Metropolis Street Racer established the central relationship that made those ideas distinctive: the road measures speed, while Kudos gives precision and style a second, persistent value.
